soft_event_news.title: Why Bank of America (BAC) is Likely to Surpass Earnings Expectations Once More - Bitget
soft_event_news.body:
If you're searching for a stock that regularly surpasses earnings expectations and may continue this trend in upcoming quarters, Bank of America (BAC) stands out as a strong contender within the Zacks Financial - Investment Bank sector.

As the nation's second-largest financial institution, Bank of America has demonstrated a pattern of exceeding earnings forecasts, particularly in its last two quarterly reports. The average earnings surprise over these periods reached 7.42%.

In the most recent quarter, Bank of America reported earnings of $0.98 per share, outpacing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.96 per share—a 2.08% surprise. The prior quarter saw an even larger beat, with actual earnings of $1.06 per share compared to an expected $0.94 per share, resulting in a 12.77% surprise.

Bank of America's upward trend in analyst estimates is partly due to its history of outperforming earnings projections. The stock's positive Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) is a strong signal for potential future earnings beats, especially when paired with a favorable Zacks Rank.

According to Zacks research, stocks that combine a positive Earnings ESP with a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) or higher tend to deliver positive earnings surprises about 70% of the time. This means that out of ten such stocks, as many as seven could exceed consensus estimates.

The Earnings ESP metric compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter. The Most Accurate Estimate reflects recent analyst revisions, often incorporating the latest information before an earnings release, which can improve accuracy over earlier consensus predictions.

Currently, Bank of America has an Earnings ESP of +1.44%, indicating increased optimism among analysts regarding its earnings outlook. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), this combination suggests another earnings beat may be forthcoming. The next earnings report is anticipated on April 15, 2026.

If the Earnings ESP is negative, it reduces the metric's predictive strength, though it does not necessarily mean the company will miss earnings expectations.

It's important to note that many companies exceed consensus EPS estimates, but this isn't always the sole driver of share price gains. Some stocks may remain steady even if they fall short of estimates.

For this reason, reviewing a company's Earnings ESP before its quarterly report can help improve investment decisions.

Zacks experts have selected five stocks they believe could increase by 100% or more in the next year. While not every pick is guaranteed to succeed, previous recommendations have achieved gains of +112%, +171%, +209%, and +232%.

Many of these stocks are not widely followed by Wall Street, offering investors a chance to invest early.
